modified_duration_balance_sheet.text: `macaulay_duration_balance_sheet` gives the Macaulay duration of a cashflow stream: the present-value-weighted average time, in years, until the cashflows arrive, using a continuous `discount_rate`. It answers "how long, on average, until this stream pays back?" `modified_duration_balance_sheet` starts from that same Macaulay figure and divides it by `1 + y/m`, where `m` is the `frequency` parameter (compounding per year, default 1). It answers "how sensitive is the value of this position to a change in the rate?" With continuous discounting (a large `frequency`), the modified figure is approximately the Macaulay one, so the two differ most when `frequency` is small. Both take `cashflows`, `times` and `discount_rate`, and only the modified version also takes `frequency`.

explain.text: `macaulay_duration_balance_sheet` (Macaulay Duration Balance Sheet) gives the Macaulay duration, in years, of a balance-sheet cashflow stream. It is the present-value-weighted average time of the cashflows, so it shows how far out the stream's value is concentrated. You supply `cashflows` (the amounts), `times` (when each occurs, in years) and `discount_rate` (a continuous rate as a decimal). Each cashflow is discounted continuously at that rate, and each time is weighted by its share of the total present value.

when.text:
Use Macaulay Duration Balance Sheet (`macaulay_duration_balance_sheet`) when you want the weighted-average timing, in years, of a stream of balance-sheet cashflows.

- You have a set of cashflow amounts (`cashflows`) with their times in years (`times`) and want a single duration figure for that stream.
- You are happy to discount continuously at one flat rate, supplied as `discount_rate` in decimal form.
- You want to see how far out the present-value-weighted cashflows sit, for example to compare the timing of assets and liabilities.
- You want the Macaulay measure specifically, not a price-sensitivity measure.

If you need the modified version of duration for a balance-sheet position, `modified_duration_balance_sheet` is listed as the related function for that.
